title: The Photograph with Six People

protagonist.name: Malati Ghosh
protagonist.coreConflict: The burden of preserving family history across twenty-four years of an unspoken property rift.

counterpart.name: Dipak Banerjee
counterpart.role: Retired tea-garden manager, Kurseong; eldest maternal cousin
counterpart.dynamic: The proud, unbending cousin who stopped speaking to Malati's father in 2000 over a terrace boundary line.

setting.secondary: The Hill Cart Road bus route through Tindharia; the cedar-lined verandah
setting.atmosphere: Cold mountain mist rolling over corrugated tin roofs, smell of pine needles and damp stone, quiet ticking of a mantle clock

signatureObjects: The 5x7 black-and-white silver gelatin print taken on June 12, 1988 on Yashica FX-3
The red clothbound album with corner mounts kept inside the steel almirah
The enamel tea kettle with chipped dark blue paint that had boiled water for all six of them in 1988
structuralMilestones: Finding the photograph wedged inside a box of tax receipts after Dipak's hospital admission
The decision to take the morning bus up the hill cart road without prior telephoning
The hesitating walk up the mossy gravel drive of Pine View Cottage
The tea served in chipped bone china while twenty-four years of silence sit between them
Looking at the photo together and recognizing that what was lost was never the land, but the laughter
